core: Integrated Earth-system processes across subsurface, surface, water and atmosphere
Mathematics, physics, chemistry, geodata, sensing, modelling and uncertainty
Field investigation, engineering design, research and societal impact

Climate dynamics, environmental change, adaptation and resilience
Earth observation, spatial data and environmental monitoring

alternatives.label: Earth systems, climate & environmental evidence
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines the strongest available UCR sequence in Earth science, climate, soils, water, resources, observation, quantitative methods and environmental research.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response to Earth, Climate and Technology: an integrated programme linking Earth processes, climate, soils, water and subsurface resources with geospatial observation, quantitative evidence and applied environmental research.

Earth/sustainability foundations support latergeoscience;math/programming precedeformalnumerical/algorithmcontinuations. Advisorysignals considered withoutinventinghardrequirements. alternatives.concept: A climate-and-observation direction organised around Earth sensing, quantitative modelling, computational analysis and geospatial evidence for environmental change and hazards.
progression: All formal prerequisites precede dependent courses and each assigned term has a current planned offering. Six-semester24-course/180EC andadvanced/PPD rules pass. alternatives.distinctness: This route makes climate sensing and computational spatial analysis the organising priority. Relative to the closest programme it replaces biodiversity, probability, remediation and ecosystem study with linear algebra, algorithms, computer vision and nature-based engineering; the pair differs by four courses and 30 EC in each direction.

alternatives.distinctness: This route makes subsurface resources and the energy transition the organising priority. Relative to the closest programme it replaces biodiversity, probability, water-management and ecosystem courses with linear algebra, linear systems, life-cycle analysis, nature-based engineering and environmental justice. trace: Sustainability Essentials I supplies physical, mathematical and systems foundations for studying linked environmental change.
Dynamic Earth directly examines structural geology, Earth history and environmental geology through laboratory and field work.
Introduction to Programming develops Python-based computational problem solving for environmental data and models.

Direct wave physics, observational methods, chemical analysis and materials stress/strain connect physical evidence to environmental and resource questions; sustainability-campaign work adds critical communication, not a general Earth-system modelling course.

Develops single-variable calculus, complex numbers, integration, differential equations and analytical/Mathematica dynamic-model investigation. These are substantive Earth-system mathematical foundations; vector/matrix methods belong to the separately selected Linear Algebra course rather than this course.
Natural Hazards, Risks & Adaptations applies geoscience to disasters, environmental change and adaptation.
Earth System Science Tools integrates Earth-system modelling, tracers, proxies and greenhouse-gas pathways.
Climate Change directly studies anthropogenic climate change, ocean acidification and climate adaptation.
Introduction to Biodiversity establishes biological diversity within the biosphere component of Earth systems.
Introduction to Data Science develops cleaning, visualisation and analysis of spatial and other datasets.
Probability & Statistics develops probability, distributions and parameter estimation for environmental evidence.

Direct ArcGIS geospatial analysis, spatial data representation and surface analysis with remote-sensing/spectral acquisition and image processing; an environmental case study applies these tools. No guaranteed drone deployment or advanced temporal geostatistics.

Direct soil properties, formation, quality, salinization and field/laboratory characterization; seismic, electrical-resistivity and electromagnetic surveys investigate soils/aquifers. Do not infer a full groundwater-flow or freshwater-resource course.
Living with Water examines flood protection, freshwater management, land subsidence and ecological consequences.
Computational & Numerical Methods develops numerical modelling, root finding and differential-equation methods.
Environmental Biogeochemistry uses geochemical modelling to analyse waters, minerals and element cycles.

Applied research process with a Zeeland sustainability partner: literature,question,investigation andfinalproduct/report. Subject and techniques depend on the project; no guaranteed geological fieldwork or international engineering design.
R3: Recycling, Recovery, Remediation applies environmental chemistry and laboratory methods to resource recovery and contamination.

Develops regression/classification, resampling, regularisation, trees, support-vector and unsupervised-learning methods with real-data projects. These are complementary methods for environmental/spatial analysis; a dedicated Earth-science dataset or project is not guaranteed.
Earth’s Resources provides advanced geoscience research on geothermal energy, subsurface carbon storage, nuclear-waste storage and responsible resource use.
Governance of Sustainability examines institutions and interests shaping climate adaptation and environmental action.
Renewable System Design develops technical and economic assessment of lower-carbon energy systems through an external-company project.
Ecosystems Uncovered directly examines ecological processes and interactions between organisms and environmental conditions.
Linear Algebra supplies vector and matrix methods used in spatial modelling and data science.
Building with Nature examines ecosystem-based design, land reclamation and flood protection.
Algorithms & Data Structures develops efficient computational methods for large and complex datasets.

Specific complementary digital-image representation,filtering,segmentation,feature detection andrecognition usingPython/OpenCV; these computational techniques can support Earth observation,without claiming dedicated remote-sensing acquisition.
Life Cycle Analysis & Circular Economy evaluates environmental impacts of technologies and resource use across complete life cycles.

Direct continuous/discrete signal and linear-system methods, Fourier/Laplace/Z transforms,sampling,filtering andfeedback. Complements geophysical sensing; no guaranteed stochastic geoscience time-series or geological model.
Social Movements & Environmental Justice examines the justice, participation and conflict dimensions of resource extraction and environmental intervention.

notes.text: TU Delft prescribes mechanics, thermodynamics, chemistry, fields and waves, fluid dynamics, atmosphere and ocean dynamics, geological engineering, geodata, international fieldwork, engineering design and a 15-EC thesis. UCR can build substantial Earth-system, climate, soils, water, resources, observation and quantitative pathways, but it does not reproduce that complete engineering-physics and field-project sequence.

selection.assessment: The closest programme covers integrated Earth systems, climate, soils, water, resources, geospatial evidence and research. Climate sensing/geospatial analysis and subsurface resources/energy responsibility form two further independently evidenced, coherent and mechanically feasible directions. All three pass the pairwise 30-EC distinctness floor, so production stops at the maximum. These are retained internal provisional concepts,not final academic approvals. Current third-year external source gate remains unresolved. Two internal course rationales are narrowed to actual calculus and generic statistical-learning content; selections,schedules andpartialalignment rows are unchanged.
